templates_considered: AUTH-010: endpoints require login. Fits only the on-call half by name; it governs app users, not developer access to prod. Rejected.
AUTH-002: admin endpoints check the caller's role. Closest to 'devs get in via admin'; still about app callers, not on-call approval. Rejected.
RET-002 / RET-001 / CONF-010: retention, audit and tagged-table access. Keyword overlap with 'prod data' only; none reads environments or copies. Rejected.
VAL-001 / CONV-060: no fit to either half of the ask. Rejected.

ask_parts_not_covered.part: Production data never ends up in staging
Devs can only get into prod through the on-call process

assumptions: 'Prod' and 'staging' are environments or tenants outside the object definitions; the workspace holds no object named for either.
The tenants table is the closest thing to deployed environments; I did not treat it as an environment marker.
confusions: The skill's 'What no check can see' section covers both halves almost verbatim, but the decision rule for 'build nothing' versus 'build a partial proxy' is not stated. I chose to build nothing, because a proxy would read as coverage it does not provide.
The brief says 'Coverage: policy files whose rules keep enforcement wired in'. With no enforcement possible, the coverage step has no object to name, so it was skipped.
wished_for: A check or statement that reads environment or branch identity, or flags copies of production data into another environment.
A check that reads an access or approval record, or ties an endpoint to an on-call approval function.
A short recipe for 'no X in Y environment' asks that says up front when to build nothing.
why_confidence: Neither half of the ask is checkable from object definitions. I built no policy, so confidence that the policy achieves the goal is low by design; the ask needs controls outside Xano policy.
